seo_title: Cliniko vs Halaxy: Australian Allied Health Software Audit (2026)
meta_description: Technical comparison of Cliniko and Halaxy for NDIS, Medicare, and Xero integration. Cliniko wins on UI/API stability; Halaxy wins on native claiming.
direct_verdict: Cliniko is the superior choice for clinics prioritizing API stability and clean UX for general practice. Halaxy is the functional winner for high-volume NDIS and Medicare providers requiring native, integrated claiming workflows.

comparison_matrix.product_b_spec: No contracts, but complex fee structures
Occasional latency during peak claim hours

product_a_pros: Superior API documentation and developer support
Transparent, predictable flat-fee pricing per practitioner
Highly stable, low-latency interface for high-volume clinics
product_a_cons: Lacks native Medicare/NDIS claiming, increasing reliance on 3rd party middleware
No free tier for small startups or solo practitioners
product_b_pros: Native, end-to-end Australian government claiming integration
Freemium entry point reduces initial capital expenditure
Deep feature set specifically tailored for NDIS reporting
product_b_cons: Complex fee structure can lead to unpredictable monthly costs
UI/UX is significantly more cluttered and slower than competitors
hidden_gotchas: Cliniko's reliance on 3rd party integrations for Medicare means you must account for the additional subscription costs of services like Medipass or Tyro, which can negate the savings of their base plan. Halaxy's 'free' model often hides costs within transaction fees and premium add-ons that are required for professional-grade reporting, leading to a higher total cost of ownership as your patient volume scales.
